features.title: ATLANTIS: THE SECRET FLIGHT
features.deck: STS-27, tile damage, and a classified shuttle mission

chapters.title: A CLASSIFIED LAUNCH
chapters.text: Atlantis rose from Kennedy Space Center on December 2 carrying a five-person crew and a classified Department of Defense payload. Secrecy limited the public account, but the launch began one of the shuttle program's most consequential early flights.

chapters.title: DAMAGE IN ORBIT
chapters.text: The crew saw extensive damage along the shuttle's right side and used the robot arm to inspect it. Poor encrypted imagery led controllers to underestimate what the astronauts were seeing.

chapters.title: A NARROW ESCAPE
chapters.text: Atlantis landed safely on December 6. Inspection revealed hundreds of damaged thermal-protection tiles; an antenna mounting plate had protected a particularly vulnerable area during reentry.

features.title: ARMENIA: EARTHQUAKE AND RELIEF
features.deck: Catastrophe, international aid, and winter recovery

chapters.title: THE GROUND BREAKS
chapters.text: A powerful earthquake struck northern Armenia on December 7, destroying buildings across Spitak, Leninakan, and surrounding communities. Winter weather and collapsed infrastructure complicated rescue work.

chapters.title: AN OPENING ACROSS BORDERS
chapters.text: The Soviet Union accepted substantial international assistance, making the relief effort a visible example of changing East-West relations during glasnost.

chapters.title: THE LONG RECOVERY
chapters.text: Emergency rescue gradually became shelter, medical care, and reconstruction. The scale of loss meant recovery would continue long after December's headlines moved elsewhere.

features.title: DIPLOMACY IN A CHANGING WORLD
features.deck: The United Nations, southern Africa, and late-Cold-War negotiation

chapters.title: GORBACHEV AT THE UNITED NATIONS
chapters.text: Mikhail Gorbachev used his December 7 address to describe reductions in Soviet armed forces and a less confrontational approach to international security.

chapters.title: NEGOTIATORS AT WORK
chapters.text: Angola, Cuba, and South Africa worked with international mediators toward an agreement linking Cuban troop withdrawal with implementation of the plan for Namibian independence.

chapters.title: THE TRIPARTITE ACCORD
chapters.text: The agreements signed on December 22 illustrated how regional conflict and superpower rivalry could yield to negotiated settlements as the Cold War entered its final years.

features.title: THE CONNECTED COMPUTER, 1988
features.deck: Modems, terminals, processors, and the pre-Web Internet

chapters.title: CALLING AN ONLINE SERVICE
chapters.text: A modem turned a telephone line into a path toward electronic mail, forums, news, and downloadable files. Connection speed and hourly charges shaped how members used every minute online.

chapters.title: POWER ON THE DESK
chapters.text: The 80386 defined the high end, while many homes and offices still relied on earlier processors. DOS software and limited memory rewarded careful configuration.

chapters.title: TEXT BEFORE THE WEB
chapters.text: Terminal screens, captured sessions, and service-specific mailboxes characterized online life. Internet standards were advancing, but the World Wide Web had not yet been proposed.

features.title: THE YEAR CLOSES
features.deck: Disaster, political change, and the uncertain end of 1988

chapters.title: LOCKERBIE
chapters.text: The destruction of Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie on December 21 killed everyone aboard and people on the ground, beginning an international investigation that would span decades.

chapters.title: TRANSITIONS AND TENSIONS
chapters.text: Elections, resignations, labor actions, and diplomatic settlements showed political systems under pressure across several regions during the month's final weeks.

chapters.title: LOOKING TOWARD 1989
chapters.text: December ended with older divisions still visible but rapid change underway. Network standards, political reform, and new diplomatic openings all pointed toward a consequential new year.
